todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (confidence 0.45): SPY closed 11-06 at 735.29, about 1.05% above its 200-day (727.64), after -5.0% in 21 days, and the Nvidia governance shock plus December hike odds keep the backdrop fragile. Held-book review (L5), using marks derived from market_value/qty (intraday, so I also give a mark 4-5% lower): BTC/USD's stored invalidation (close more than 10% below the 83,685.83 fill, about 75,317) has tripped. The 11-06 close was 74,756, and BTC broke below $75K again this morning with ETF outflows. The exchange-failure clause is untripped (no exchange failed in the News input). The Skeptic's case against P1 is weak and I agree: the rule was written in advance, the position is about $13, and 'local bottom' is opinion. I approve selling in full (P1). L1 and L5 applied. P2 (VNQ): the Skeptic's serious objection holds up. This is the most rate-sensitive equity sleeve, bought into a week of inflation reports with December hike odds elevated, after a 21-day bounce (63d is -0.57%). A 0.315 beta understates its sensitivity to a rates shock, and the Market Analyst expects little appetite for adding equity risk. The Implicator found it small and diversifying (about 3.2% of equity at $20), and the Real Estate tilt is a Market Analyst favourite, so I do not reject it. But the owner wants the account mostly invested and cash is 11.4%, so I shrink it to a trial $12 rather than $20 (L4: that is about 1.9% of equity, justified by the Real Estate tilt and the low-beta diversification, not diversification alone). That is roughly the BTC proceeds, so the buy is close to a swap, not new risk, and cash stays near 11.6%, above the 10% buffer ($61.82) even if the BTC sale fills a little low. Orders should run sell first, then buy. The stance is risk-off and SPY sits 1% above the line, so I add no equity beta and no other new names today; INCY stays the first candidate if cash rises and the tape steadies. Other held names, distance to stop on the current mark and on a mark 4-5% lower: VOO/VTI invalidate on SPY below its 200-day (727.64, 1.05% away; a 4-5% lower SPY would breach it, and the code regime filter would then switch off buys and I would reassess at that close); IDXX about 676 vs 630 (about 7% away, about 2% on a mark 5% lower, about $2.4 of dollar risk to the stop at current weight, no earnings until 2027-02-01); MSM about 113.8 vs roughly 108 (about 5% away, so a 5% lower mark would reach the stop, position is only about $7.7); BND about 71.6 vs 70.0 (2.2%) and IEF about 92 vs 89.5 (2.6%), the nearest stops, both small and rate-exposed with inflation data this week; CARG about 33.7 vs 28.25 (16% away); DPZ about 336 vs 285; WMT, KR, MSCI, FAST, VRSN all 10%+ from their stops. No held name has earnings inside 5 trading days (WMT 11-19, KR 12-03). DPZ's guidance-cut item remains unconfirmed. Staples (WMT, DPZ, KR) are still about 26% by label and I am not adding (L3). I am only re-anchoring the VOO and VTI SPY line to the current 727.64 reading.

trades.thesis: Stop rule firing, not a new view: the 11-06 close (74,756) is below the stored invalidation of 10% under the 83,685.83 fill (about 75,317), BTC broke below $75K again this morning with ETF outflows, and the 11-11 MSCI decision and this week's inflation data are further downside catalysts. The loss (about $1.60, short-term) is realized; the position is only about $13.
trades.invalidation: The sale is wrong if BTC/USD closes back above about 80,000 within 5 sessions; do not rebuy BTC before about 2026-12-09 (wash-sale window).

trades.thesis: Trial real-estate sleeve in the one area the Market Analyst both favors and sees trending (VNQ 21d +7.14%, 2.48% above its 200-day, vol 14%, beta about 0.3), with no held REIT and no addition to the Technology or Consumer Staples stacks. Resized from $20 to $12: the Skeptic is right that it is rate-sensitive going into inflation reports and December hike odds, that part of the 21-day move is a bounce, and that the cash buffer is tight if the BTC sale fills low. Funded roughly by the BTC proceeds.
trades.invalidation: VNQ closes more than about 5% below the actual fill (about $90.5 if it fills near the 95.73 reference close; re-anchor to the real fill per L1), or a hot inflation print pushes TLT more than 3% below its 200-day while the Market Analyst turns risk-off on real estate.

DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes below $285 (10% under the $316.58 actual fill), or a fundamentals screen drops it from the menu or shows cfo below net income, or a confirmed guidance cut
DPZ.update_why: The stored $274.88 stop was anchored to the $305.42 pre-fill reference close, so it sat about 13% under the fill. Re-anchored to the fill (L1).

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name in a favored sector (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.949, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, no added leverage or dilution). The 11-02 print beat and raised guidance (stock about +20%); no earnings until 2027-02-01. Executives sold over $27M of stock after the run, a mild sentiment negative. Sized down because its 0.787 beta makes it the least defensive holding in the book.
IDXX.invalidation: close below $630 (about 10% under the ~$700 mark, still about 13% above the $555.81 fill), or IDXX underperforms XLV by more than 5 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window

WMT.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
WMT.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.

The Skeptic and Implicator note it largely duplicates VOO and raises beta, and that small caps are weak, so I buy a smaller tranche and hold back the rest given the risk-off open. Resulting US broad-ETF weight is about 18.4%.

VTI.update_why: Same re-anchor as VOO: the stored 727.38 line is the 11-05 reading, the current line is 727.64.

FAST.thesis: Lowest volatility on the menu (0.243), F-score 8/9, gross profitability at the 89th sector percentile, and operating cash flow above net income. It adds a first Consumer Discretionary exposure, not overlapping the staples names held. Resized from $40: the Skeptic is right that its earnings date was never verified, that cash conversion is only about 1.03x, and that the sector label may flatter it. The Implicator confirmed the diversification claim holds.
FAST.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an earnings report showing operating cash flow clearly below net income.

CARG.thesis: Rank 4 on fundamentals (gross profitability 1.27, cfo about 1.9x net income, beta 0.44), held as one combined position at about 5.6% of equity and +14.7% on cost. The 11-05 print is out: Q3 adj EPS $0.70 vs $0.66, sales $258.4M vs $256.5M, FY26 EPS guide raised to $2.66-$2.72, $250M buyback; Q4 sales guide midpoint slightly below the estimate. Numbers are mixed-to-positive and the negative-surprise clause is retired. No earnings event ahead.

CARG.update_why: The earnings clause is stale now that the print has happened and was not negative on the numbers; the price stop stays.

KR.thesis: Staples is a Market Analyst favored sector, KR has low event risk (next earnings 12-03, the 10-20 8-K was an investor-day update) and the sell side is supportive after the 7-11% EPS CAGR target. The Skeptic and Implicator are right that this stacks on WMT and DPZ (staples about 22.5% of equity) and that the negative beta is a statistical artifact, so I take a smaller position, which lifts staples only to about 25.9%.
KR.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price, or the 10-17 grocery-chain cyber incident is confirmed to be Kroger, or a guidance cut at the 12-03 print.

The Skeptic is right that the sector label is Industrials (not a favored sector) and that the post-print re-rating is partly priced, so I trim the size and rest the case on quality and diversification only.

Bond weight stops here: no further bond adds without a post-Fed reassessment.
